items.title: Bobby Watson interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, January 19, 1996
items.q: That’s like telling Ali to box like Frasier.

ctx.x: goes, “Let me try it.” And he put this whole other beat on it and took it somewhere else. And my eyes, I said okay, the little light bulb went off, you know? How stupid I am trying to tell Art Blakey to play it kind of Elvinish. You know I mean he’s an institution of himself, Elvin, and so is Art. And you know if you’ve got Art, you take Art, you don’t want — you want Elvin [Jones], you go get Elvin.
That’s like telling Ali to box like Frasier.

Yeah. You want me, you got me. And so I never wrote drum parts out again, and I still don’t to this day. I may give a trumpet part. And so that’s why this improvisation you’re saying begins immediately when you have artists that are in that spirit of creating so that when they’re comping, they’re actually playing little counter melodies and there’s this voice leading and all the chords, and if you just take away all the chords and just listen to what’s on top, you should hear the little counter melodies flowing…
